title: UL-19 — Challenge: EKS control plane then delete
scenario: Add Fargate profile or one node group to EKS, then remove before cluster delete.
acceptanceCriteria: Name the resources you create `workbook-ul19`: cluster `workbook-ul19` in the default VPC (as in GL-19), role `workbook-ul19-eks`, and either node group `workbook-ul19-ng` with role `workbook-ul19-node` or Fargate profile `workbook-ul19-fp` with role `workbook-ul19-fargate`. Tag each one LabId=ul-19.
Either Fargate profile OR one managed node group added briefly.
kubectl get nodes shows Ready once if node path chosen.
Node group scaled to zero or Fargate profile removed before cluster delete.
IAM roles cleaned after cluster delete.
CloudWatch log groups for cluster removed if enabled.

hints.text: Fargate profiles need private subnets; the default VPC (like GL-19) has only public ones, so most learners pick the node group path. EKS also rejects subnets in AZ ID use1-az3; pick default-VPC subnets by availability-zone-id, as GL-19 does.
Fargate profile delete can take minutes.
Control plane bills until cluster gone.

stopChargesPanel: Delete the node group or Fargate profile and wait, delete the EKS cluster and wait, then the cluster log group and the ul-19 IAM roles.

orderedDeletesPowerShell: # Uses: none (resources are named workbook-ul19)
# Lost track? List what is left: aws resourcegroupstaggingapi get-resources --tag-filters Key=LabId,Values=ul-19
# Node groups and Fargate profiles must be gone before delete-cluster. Each delete waits (node groups can take 10+ minutes).

foreach ($Ng in ((aws eks list-nodegroups --cluster-name workbook-ul19 --query nodegroups --output text) -split '\s+')) { if ($Ng -and $Ng -ne 'None') { aws eks delete-nodegroup --cluster-name workbook-ul19 --nodegroup-name $Ng --query nodegroup.status --output text; aws eks wait nodegroup-deleted --cluster-name workbook-ul19 --nodegroup-name $Ng } }

foreach ($Fp in ((aws eks list-fargate-profiles --cluster-name workbook-ul19 --query fargateProfileNames --output text) -split '\s+')) { if ($Fp -and $Fp -ne 'None') { aws eks delete-fargate-profile --cluster-name workbook-ul19 --fargate-profile-name $Fp --query fargateProfile.status --output text; aws eks wait fargate-profile-deleted --cluster-name workbook-ul19 --fargate-profile-name $Fp } }
aws eks delete-cluster --name workbook-ul19 --query cluster.status --output text
aws eks wait cluster-deleted --name workbook-ul19
$LogGroup = aws logs describe-log-groups --log-group-name-prefix /aws/eks/workbook-ul19/cluster --query "logGroups[?logGroupName=='/aws/eks/workbook-ul19/cluster'].logGroupName | [0]" --output text
if ($LogGroup -and $LogGroup -ne 'None') { aws logs delete-log-group --log-group-name $LogGroup }
# IAM roles after the cluster is gone; roles you did not create are skipped
$EksRole = aws iam list-roles --query "Roles[?RoleName=='workbook-ul19-eks'].RoleName | [0]" --output text

if ($EksRole -and $EksRole -ne 'None') { foreach ($P in (aws iam list-attached-role-policies --role-name workbook-ul19-eks --query "AttachedPolicies[].[PolicyArn]" --output text)) { if ($P) { aws iam detach-role-policy --role-name workbook-ul19-eks --policy-arn $P } } }

if ($EksRole -and $EksRole -ne 'None') { foreach ($P in ((aws iam list-role-policies --role-name workbook-ul19-eks --query PolicyNames --output text) -split '\s+')) { if ($P -and $P -ne 'None') { aws iam delete-role-policy --role-name workbook-ul19-eks --policy-name $P } } }
if ($EksRole -and $EksRole -ne 'None') { aws iam delete-role --role-name workbook-ul19-eks }
$NodeRole = aws iam list-roles --query "Roles[?RoleName=='workbook-ul19-node'].RoleName | [0]" --output text

if ($NodeRole -and $NodeRole -ne 'None') { foreach ($P in (aws iam list-attached-role-policies --role-name workbook-ul19-node --query "AttachedPolicies[].[PolicyArn]" --output text)) { if ($P) { aws iam detach-role-policy --role-name workbook-ul19-node --policy-arn $P } } }

if ($NodeRole -and $NodeRole -ne 'None') { foreach ($P in ((aws iam list-role-policies --role-name workbook-ul19-node --query PolicyNames --output text) -split '\s+')) { if ($P -and $P -ne 'None') { aws iam delete-role-policy --role-name workbook-ul19-node --policy-name $P } } }
if ($NodeRole -and $NodeRole -ne 'None') { aws iam delete-role --role-name workbook-ul19-node }
$FargateRole = aws iam list-roles --query "Roles[?RoleName=='workbook-ul19-fargate'].RoleName | [0]" --output text

if ($FargateRole -and $FargateRole -ne 'None') { foreach ($P in (aws iam list-attached-role-policies --role-name workbook-ul19-fargate --query "AttachedPolicies[].[PolicyArn]" --output text)) { if ($P) { aws iam detach-role-policy --role-name workbook-ul19-fargate --policy-arn $P } } }

if ($FargateRole -and $FargateRole -ne 'None') { foreach ($P in ((aws iam list-role-policies --role-name workbook-ul19-fargate --query PolicyNames --output text) -split '\s+')) { if ($P -and $P -ne 'None') { aws iam delete-role-policy --role-name workbook-ul19-fargate --policy-name $P } } }
if ($FargateRole -and $FargateRole -ne 'None') { aws iam delete-role --role-name workbook-ul19-fargate }
verification: aws resourcegroupstaggingapi get-resources --tag-filters Key=LabId,Values=ul-19 returns an empty ResourceTagMappingList in $env:AWS_REGION
aws eks describe-cluster --name workbook-ul19 returns ResourceNotFoundException
aws iam get-role --role-name workbook-ul19-eks returns NoSuchEntity
teardown.stillBillingNote: Time already used, transfer, tax, and 8–12h billing lag may still appear. Alerts do not delete resources.
teardown.recovery: If teardown fails, stop. Confirm $env:AWS_REGION is us-east-1 and the caller is not root. Run aws sts get-caller-identity and type that Account value before any delete. List LabId=ul-19 with aws resourcegroupstaggingapi get-resources --tag-filters Key=LabId,Values=ul-19. Delete only those ids. Never delete untagged resources. If delete-cluster returns ResourceInUseException, a node group or Fargate profile still exists: rerun those two lines and let each wait finish.

beforeYouStart: Read the paired guided lab (gl-19) stop-charges panel before you create anything.
Set $env:AWS_PROFILE and $env:AWS_REGION. Do not use the root user.
